top_choice_rationale: Optical lattice clocks (Katori, Ye) are a bounded achievement with a two-name proposal-plus-realisation credit and more than two decades of independent reproduction in Sr, Yb and Hg. The magic-wavelength condition is a distinct principle, because it removes the first-order light shift for many atoms and changes the quantum-projection-noise regime, and is not just a better implementation of the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control toolkit. P001 is second because the Z2 state and its first observation are mature and conceptually important, but the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang step linking theory to experiment sits outside the three names, so I would accept it only with an explicit citation. P002 has the cleanest theory-to-experiment chain, but seven years of confirmation with the pairing mechanism unsettled makes it less mature. No award is last because mature, well-confirmed discoveries are available.
recusal_note: Possible recusal ground on P003: I spent a research stay in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder, and JILA is Jun Ye's home institution. My profile documents no collaboration with Katori or Ye, and I also have field proximity in precision atomic physics. No specific connection to the names in P001 or P002 is apparent from my profile.
